additions.reason: The source text explicitly calls Jacob's act of making converts a 'בְּחִינַת מְגוּרֵי אָבִיו' — an aspect of 'the sojournings of his father'. The word מְגוּרֵי (sojournings) is re-read midrashically as גִּיּוּרֵי (conversions), equating the patriarchal mission of bringing souls close to God with Jacob's continuation of that work. This is the one explicit bechina equation in the Torah. It is not in the dataset. Because there are no existing packages for Torah 228, a suggested package cannot be assigned a numeric id.
additions.source_quote: הַיְנוּ מֵחֲמַת שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב הָיָה מְגַיֵּר גֵּרִים, בְּחִינַת מְגוּרֵי אָבִיו

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: מְגוּרֵי אָבִיו (the sojournings / conversions of his father — bechina of Jacob making gerim)
מַחֲלֹקֶת (controversy/opposition — structural condition, eitza not bechina)
גֵּרִים (converts — the subject of the teaching, no bechina label applied to them directly)
שַׁלְוָה (tranquility — mentioned as the thing Jacob sought but could not have; no bechina label)
רֻגְזוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף (the anguish of Joseph — mentioned as the machlokes that fell on Jacob; no bechina label)

bechina_language_occurrences_in_source_t.explanation: Jacob's convert-making is called an aspect of 'the sojournings of his father'. The only explicit bechina equation in the Torah.
